messages:
jin: Quick RFC follow-up — experiment idea: make the policy "evaluator" plane fully pluggable via WASM modules that implement scoring predicates. Thoughts on safety/observability tradeoffs?

mike: curious. how would the contract look? scorer returns single score or richer signal?

jin: MVP contract proposal: function score(request_meta, route_meta) -> {score: float, reason: string} (0..1). Keep it tiny to make deterministic unit tests easy.

elaine: +1 for small contract. main concern is startup latency for many tenants with custom modules (cold instantiation). we need warm pool semantics or lazy compile.

samir: also think about failure modes — if a tenant's WASM crashes, we must have a deterministic fallback. fallback to built-in JS scorer plus circuit breaker.

jin: agreed. fallback plan: 1) runtime sandbox kills bad wasm 2) mark module degraded 3) route to default scorer. Ops-visible event and metric.

rachael: telemetry ask: we need per-eval timing, gc pressure, and a histogram of score distributions. Also record decision_reasons (sparse) for debugging eval drift.

mike: implementation tradeoffs: embed Wasmtime vs use a remote scoring service per-tenant. Wasmtime -> lower p95, remote service -> easier debug & hotpatching.

jin: we benchmarked a PoC last week: single-threaded Wasm scorer ~120µs per eval (including sandbox overhead) on our standard instance, remote RPC ~650µs median. numbers vary with payload size.

elaine: 120µs is good but if we batch and do continuous scoring for large batches, wasm single-threaded could become a bottleneck. need to allow multi-instance pools or shared workers.

samir: what about expressiveness? Some policies need graph lookups (tenant affinity, recent failures). WASM only with read-only runtime state is fine, but not for calls to distributed stores.

jin: plan: keep scoring pure and side-effect free. Provide read-only snapshot of required signals (recent latency buckets, capacity tags) passed as request_meta. Any external lookups are done by the control plane prepopulating signals.

rachael: that implies we must extend telemetry ingestion to maintain short-lived signal windows per tenant. ops cost increase — quantify.

mike: interface question: how do we express fallbacks/ordering? Do modules return "ineligible" vs small score? I prefer explicit statuses: {status: "ok"|"ineligible"|"error", score, reason}.

jin: OK. update contract to include status. simple statuses keep runtime logic readable.

ops-bot: deploy: canary/wasm-scorer v1 deployed to canary cluster at 2139876600.

mike: rollout plan idea: canary 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with auto-rollback on score-distribution drift or increased tail latency. Keep an automated inspector job that compares routing decisions vs baseline for a sample of requests.

samir: add deterministic replay harness: record inputs at canary and replay them through built-in scorer to make sure behavior is explainable.

jin: action items: @mike design pool manager (warm pools, concurrency limits), @elaine cost model for signal windows, @samir failure & fallback flows + test harness, @rachael telemetry schema and incidence alerts. I'll drive the RFC update with the new contract and PoC numbers.

rachael: can we get a small policy DSL example for docs? e.g.:
```
# example wasm policy input (JSON)
{
  "region": "eu-west-1",
  "latency_p50_ms": 22,
  "tenant_priority": 50
}

# pseudo scorer logic
if region != "eu-west-1": return {status: "ineligible", score: 0, reason: "region-mismatch"}
score = sigmoid((100 - tenant_priority) / 100) * exp(-latency_p50_ms/100)
return {status: "ok", score: score, reason: "composite"}
```

mike: nice. keep DSL examples in RFC, but enforce that wasm implementations are deterministic and pure (no clocks/randomness).

jin: thanks. I'll update RFC and schedule a short sync next Tuesday to walk the PoC & rollout plan.

elaine: +1. please include cost estimates for per-tenant signal windows; that will be the main blocker for many customers.

samir: also add an operator mode that forbids tenant-supplied modules globally (enterprise control).

jin: noted. I'll add enterprise guardrail and KV flag to opt-out.

rachael: tagging follow-ups: telemetry dashboards, alert thresholds, canary replay harness.

mike: tagging infra: container/cgroup limits for Wasm runtime, warm-pool autoscaler knobs.

jin: great. thanks all — will post RFC patch 2139880000 and link back here.
